backup.section.title: Notebox backup
backup.section.intro: Periodically creates a zip archive (with optional encryption) of the currently in-use notebox to a destination of your choice. Backups run while the app is open. You can create ad-hoc backups, manually from the command palette ({modifier} + P → “Back up notebox now”).
backup.enabled.label: Notebox backup & restore
backup.enabled.description: When off, scheduled backups don't run and the manual command is disabled. Your destination folder and other settings are retained. Turn on to enable backups or restore files from a backup.
backup.destination.label: Destination folder
backup.destination.description: Where archives are written. If empty, backups will be disabled.
backup.destination.cannotUseNotebox: Cannot use the notebox folder (or a subfolder of it) as a backup destination — backups would archive themselves.
backup.interval.label: Backup interval (hours)
backup.interval.description: How often to back up while the app is running. 0 disables scheduled backups (manual runs still work).
backup.keepCount.label: Retain this many backups
backup.keepCount.description: Older archives matching the filename pattern are pruned after each successful backup.
backup.onlyOnChange.label: Only back up when something changed
backup.onlyOnChange.description: Skip the scheduled backup if no notebox file has been modified since the last successful run. Manual runs always proceed.
backup.includeUserConfig.label: Include user settings folder
backup.includeUserConfig.description: Bundle your global InkyCap settings (theme, fonts, creation rules, bookmarks) alongside the notebox. Useful when restoring on a new machine.
backup.filenamePattern.label: Filename pattern
backup.filenamePattern.description: Template for each archive. Tokens: {tokens}. Reserved characters are replaced with _.
backup.password.label: Password protection (optional)
backup.password.description: When set, archives will be encrypted with AES-256. InkyCap will attempt to store the password in your OS keychain. It will not write it in the settings file or elsewhere. Keep track of it.
backup.password.perArchiveNotice: The password is bound to each archive at the moment it is created. Changing or clearing the password here affects only the next backup. Existing archives keep the password they were made with so you must use that particular password to restore them.
backup.password.unrecoverableWarning: ⚠ If you lose this password, the backup becomes unrecoverable. There is no reset.
backup.password.saved: Password saved to OS keychain. Future backups will use this password; existing archives keep their original password.
backup.password.cleared: Password cleared. Future backups will be unencrypted. Existing encrypted archives still need their original password to restore.
backup.password.confirmChangeBody: This new password will be used for future backups only. Existing archives remain encrypted with the password they were made with, and you'll need that particular password to restore them. Continue?
backup.password.confirmClearBody: Future backups will no longer be encrypted. Existing encrypted archives still need their original password to restore. Clearing the keychain does not unlock them. Continue?
backup.lastBackup.label: Last backup
backup.runNow.paletteHint: Or trigger from the command palette ({modifier} + P → “Back up notebox now”).
backup.toast.skipped: Backup skipped (no changes since last run).
backup.browse.title: Browse backups
backup.browse.intro: Choose a backup archive to restore your entire notebox or selected files.
backup.browse.noArchives: No backup archives found in the destination folder yet.
backup.browse.targetOriginalDisabled: Open a notebox to restore in place
backup.browse.passwordHint: Each archive is encrypted with the password that was active when it was created. The current password from the OS keychain is used by default; type a different password here only if this archive was made with one. Leave empty to use the keychain.
backup.browse.noPassword: This archive is encrypted. No password is set in the OS keychain — type the password the archive was created with before restoring.
